shared.commonMistake: Focus on the semantic element and the required attributes first. Your visible text can be personal unless the task asks for exact machine-readable values such as ids, URLs, names, or dates.
shared.bestPractice: Build the smallest valid HTML that proves the {topic} idea first, then personalize visible text once the semantic structure is correct.

html-semantic-paragraph.title: Wrap meaning in a tag
html-semantic-paragraph.summary:
HTML is semantic: tags describe what content means. A paragraph is not just text on a new line;

tells the browser this content is a paragraph.
html-semantic-paragraph.objective:
Inside body, create one paragraph element with any text inside it. Use an opening

tag and a matching closing

tag.
html-semantic-paragraph.hint: Use an opening p tag and a closing p tag around a short sentence of your own.
checks: A paragraph element with text exists in body

html-paired-tags.title: Close what you open
html-paired-tags.summary: Paired tags must be closed in the right place. Closing tags tell the browser where an element ends.
html-paired-tags.objective:
Create two separate paragraph elements. Each paragraph must have its own opening

tag and closing

tag.
html-paired-tags.hint: Write two sibling paragraphs, not one paragraph containing another paragraph.
checks: Two paragraph elements with text exist

html-nesting.title: Nest tags correctly
html-nesting.summary: Elements can live inside other elements. Correct nesting means the inner element opens and closes before the outer element closes.
html-nesting.objective: Create one paragraph and use strong around one meaningful word or phrase inside it.
html-nesting.hint: Keep the strong element inside the paragraph, then write your own sentence around it.
checks: Strong text is nested inside a paragraph

html-emphasis.title: Choose meaning over appearance
html-emphasis.summary: Semantic inline elements explain meaning. em means stressed emphasis; it is not just a way to make text italic.
html-emphasis.objective: Create a paragraph that uses em around one stressed word or phrase you choose.
html-emphasis.hint: Put the em element inside a paragraph, around the word or phrase that should be stressed.
checks: Emphasis is nested inside a paragraph

html-heading-paragraph.title: Add a page heading
html-heading-paragraph.summary: Headings create a content outline. h1 is usually the main heading for the page or current view.
html-heading-paragraph.objective: Create one h1 heading and one paragraph after it. The text can be yours, but both elements must contain something.
checks: Heading appears before paragraph in body

html-document-title.title: Name the browser tab
html-document-title.summary: head contains metadata for the browser. body contains the content people see on the page.
html-document-title.objective: Change the title element in head to a page-specific title, then keep a visible h1 in body.
html-document-title.hint: Edit the existing title in head, then add a visible heading in body. The title and heading text can be yours.

html-attributes.title: Add details with attributes
html-attributes.summary: Attributes add extra information to an element. Some attributes configure behavior; others provide names or reusable hooks.
html-attributes.objective: Create a section with a non-empty id and at least two class names. Add any text inside it.
html-attributes.hint: Put id and class on the opening section tag. Separate multiple class names with spaces.
checks: Section has at least two classes

html-comments.title: Leave a useful source note
html-comments.summary: Comments explain intent to people reading the source. They are not rendered as visible page content.
html-comments.objective: Add an HTML comment before a main element to describe the main content region.
html-comments.hint: Use HTML comment syntax before main. Comments start with <!-- and end with -->.

html-entities.title: Show reserved characters
html-entities.summary: Some characters have special meaning in HTML source. Character references let you display them as text.
html-entities.objective: Inside a paragraph, display a less-than sign and an ampersand as text by using entities for < and &.
html-entities.hint: Use < for a visible less-than sign and & for a visible ampersand inside a paragraph.
checks: Less-than entity is inside a paragraph
Ampersand entity is inside a paragraph

html-link.title: Create a meaningful link
html-link.summary: Links connect documents. The href attribute stores the destination; the text should tell users where the link goes.
html-link.objective: Create an anchor linking to https://developer.mozilla.org/. Put any visible text inside the link.
html-link.hint: Use an a element with href="https://developer.mozilla.org/".

html-image-alt.title: Describe an image
html-image-alt.summary: Images need alternative text so their meaning remains available when the image cannot be seen or loaded.
html-image-alt.objective: Add an image with a non-empty src and a non-empty alt attribute.
html-image-alt.hint: The src points to the image file. The alt text should describe the image purpose in your own words.

html-button.title: Mark an action as a button
html-button.summary: button represents an action. An explicit type prevents accidental form submission later.
html-button.objective: Create a button with type="button" and any visible text.
html-button.hint: Use <button type="button">Start lesson</button> or another clear label.

html-lang-meta.title: Describe the document
html-lang-meta.summary: Document metadata helps browsers, search engines, translators, and assistive technology understand the page.
html-lang-meta.objective: Make sure html has lang="en", head has UTF-8 charset, and head has a responsive viewport meta tag.
html-lang-meta.hint: Put lang on html and both meta elements inside head.

html-page-regions.title: Create page regions
html-page-regions.summary: Landmark elements divide a page into major regions. They make the structure easier for people and assistive technology to navigate.
html-page-regions.objective: Create header, main, and footer elements in that order inside body. Put a little text in each region.
html-page-regions.hint: Place the three elements as siblings inside body.

html-navigation.title: Build primary navigation
html-navigation.summary: nav identifies a major set of navigation links. A label distinguishes this navigation from other nav regions.
html-navigation.objective: Create a nav with a non-empty aria-label containing links to / and /lessons.
html-navigation.hint: Give nav an aria-label that names this navigation region, then nest the two links inside it.

html-main-article.title: Wrap independent content
html-main-article.summary: article is for content that makes sense as a self-contained piece, such as a post, lesson, card, or news item.
html-main-article.objective: Inside main, create an article with one h1 and one paragraph.
html-main-article.hint: Nest article inside main, then nest h1 and p inside article.
checks: Main contains an article with heading and paragraph

html-sections.title: Split content into sections
html-sections.summary: section groups a themed part of a document. A section normally needs a heading that explains its topic.
html-sections.objective: Create an article containing two section elements. Each section should have an h2.
html-sections.hint: Put two section elements inside article, and put an h2 in each section.

html-aside.title: Add supporting content
html-aside.summary: aside represents related but secondary content, such as a tip, callout, sidebar, or related link list.
html-aside.objective: Inside main, add an article and an aside. The aside should contain a short tip.
html-aside.hint: Put both article and aside inside main.

html-unordered-list.title: Group related items
html-unordered-list.summary: Unordered lists group items where sequence does not matter.
html-unordered-list.objective: Create a ul containing at least three li items for things someone can learn.
html-unordered-list.hint: Nest three li elements inside one ul.
checks: Unordered list contains at least three items

html-ordered-list.title: Describe ordered steps
html-ordered-list.summary: Ordered lists communicate sequence, ranking, or procedure. Source order matters.
html-ordered-list.objective: Create an ol with at least three li items that describe steps in a process you choose.
html-ordered-list.hint: Use one ol and put each step in its own li. Ordered lists communicate sequence through source order.
checks: Ordered list contains at least three written steps

html-description-list.title: Define terms
html-description-list.summary: Description lists pair terms with descriptions, metadata names with values, or question-and-answer style content.
html-description-list.objective: Create a dl with at least two dt terms and two dd descriptions.
html-description-list.hint: Use dt for each term and dd for the description that follows it.
checks: Description list contains at least two terms and descriptions

html-figure.title: Caption media
html-figure.summary: figure groups self-contained media with an optional caption. figcaption explains the figure.
html-figure.objective: Create a figure containing an image with a non-empty src and a meaningful figcaption.
html-figure.hint: Nest img and figcaption inside figure.
checks: Figure contains the image and caption together

html-blockquote.title: Quote another source
html-blockquote.summary: blockquote represents a longer quotation from another source. cite can point to the source URL.
html-blockquote.objective: Create a blockquote with cite="https://developer.mozilla.org/" and at least one paragraph inside.
html-blockquote.hint: Nest a p element inside blockquote.

html-time.title: Make dates machine-readable
html-time.summary: time connects human-readable text with a standardized value software can parse.
html-time.objective: Create a time element with a YYYY-MM-DD datetime value and visible date text.
html-time.hint: Put datetime on the opening time tag.

html-details.title: Create native disclosure
html-details.summary: details and summary provide disclosure behavior without JavaScript.
html-details.objective: Create details with a summary question and a paragraph answer.
html-details.hint: Put summary first inside details, then a paragraph.
checks: Disclosure contains summary first and a paragraph answer

html-address.title: Mark contact information
html-address.summary: address represents contact information for the nearest article or page.
html-address.objective: Create an address element containing a mailto link to hello@example.com.
html-address.hint: Put an a element with href="mailto:hello@example.com" inside address.

html-form-label.title: Label a form control
html-form-label.summary: Labels give form controls an accessible name and a larger clickable target.
html-form-label.objective: Create a text input and connect it to a visible label with matching for and id values.
html-form-label.hint: Choose an id for the input, then use the same value in the label for attribute.
checks: Label is connected to the text input

html-form-submit.title: Submit a form
html-form-submit.summary: form groups controls and defines where and how values are submitted.
html-form-submit.objective: Create a form that posts to a non-empty action URL with an email input and a submit button.
html-form-submit.hint: Put action and method on form, then nest the email input and submit button inside it.
checks: Signup form contains the email field and submit button

html-input-types.title: Choose input types
html-input-types.summary: Specific input types give browsers validation hints and better mobile keyboards.
html-input-types.objective: Inside a form, add required email and password inputs. Give each input a non-empty name.
html-input-types.hint: Use the email and password input types, add required, and include name values so the form can submit data.

html-textarea-select.title: Collect longer and fixed answers
html-textarea-select.summary: textarea collects multi-line text. select limits users to known option values.
html-textarea-select.objective: Create a labelled textarea with rows="4" and a labelled select with at least two options.
html-textarea-select.hint: Connect labels with for/id, give each control a name, and put option elements inside select.
checks: Textarea is labelled and has rows
Select is labelled and contains at least two options

html-fieldsets.title: Group related choices
html-fieldsets.summary: fieldset groups related controls. legend gives the group an accessible name.
html-fieldsets.objective: Group at least two radio buttons in a fieldset with a visible legend.
html-fieldsets.hint: Place legend first, then add labelled radio inputs that share a meaningful name.
checks: Fieldset contains a legend and at least two labelled radios with the same name

html-checkbox.title: Represent an agreement
html-checkbox.summary: Checkboxes represent independent on/off choices and can be required before submission.
html-checkbox.objective: Create a required checkbox with a name, an id, and a visible label connected to it.
html-checkbox.hint: Choose an id for the checkbox, then use the same value in the label for attribute.
checks: Required checkbox has id and name

html-validation.title: Add native validation
html-validation.summary: Native constraint attributes establish a useful first validation layer in the browser. Server validation is still required.
html-validation.objective: Create a named input with required, minlength, maxlength, and pattern constraints.
html-validation.hint: Put all constraints on one input. Use numeric minlength and maxlength values, and write a non-empty pattern.

html-autocomplete.title: Support autofill
html-autocomplete.summary: autocomplete tokens tell browsers what a field represents so they can fill it accurately.
html-autocomplete.objective: Add a personal-name input and an email input with autocomplete="name" and autocomplete="email". Give both fields a non-empty name attribute.
html-autocomplete.hint: Match each input purpose with the correct autocomplete token.

html-table.title: Build a data table
html-table.summary: Tables express relationships in genuinely tabular data. They should not be used for page layout.
html-table.objective: Create a table with at least two header cells and at least two data cells.
html-table.hint: Use table, tr, th, and td.
checks: Table contains header and data rows

html-table-scope.title: Clarify table headers
html-table-scope.summary: caption names a table. scope helps assistive technology connect headers to cells.
html-table-scope.objective: Create a table with a visible caption and at least two column headers that use scope="col".
html-table-scope.hint: Put caption inside table, then add th elements with scope.
checks: Table contains caption and scoped column headers

html-audio.title: Provide audio with fallback
html-audio.summary: audio embeds sound. source provides media candidates. Fallback text helps when the element is unsupported.
html-audio.objective: Create an audio element with controls, a source with type audio/mpeg, and fallback text.
html-audio.hint: Nest source and fallback text inside audio.
checks: Audio element contains its MPEG source and fallback text

html-video.title: Add video captions
html-video.summary: Videos need captions so spoken content is available without audio.
html-video.objective: Create a video with controls, a source, and a captions track with srclang="en".
html-video.hint: Nest source and track inside video.
checks: Video contains source and English captions track

html-picture.title: Offer responsive image choices
html-picture.summary: picture lets the browser choose from different image sources for different conditions.
html-picture.objective: Create a picture with a source for min-width screens and an img fallback with non-empty src and alt text.
html-picture.hint: Put source first and img last inside picture.
checks: Picture contains the wide source and fallback image

html-skip-link.title: Let keyboard users skip navigation
html-skip-link.summary: Skip links help keyboard and assistive technology users bypass repeated navigation.
html-skip-link.objective: Create a skip link before header that points to the id of the main content.
html-skip-link.hint: Choose an id for main, then make the skip link href use # followed by that same id.
checks: Skip link appears before header and main

html-aria-current.title: Mark the current page
html-aria-current.summary: aria-current tells assistive technology which item in a set represents the current page or step.
html-aria-current.objective: Inside a nav, create a link to / and mark it with aria-current="page".
html-aria-current.hint: Put aria-current on the anchor that represents the current page.
checks: Current page link is inside navigation

html-aria-expanded.title: Expose control state
html-aria-expanded.summary: ARIA can expose state and relationships when native HTML does not already provide them.
html-aria-expanded.objective: Create a button with aria-expanded="false" and aria-controls pointing to a target element id.
html-aria-expanded.hint: Choose an id for the controlled content, then use the same value in the button aria-controls attribute.

html-progress-meter.title: Represent measured values
html-progress-meter.summary: progress represents task completion. meter represents a scalar measurement within a known range.
html-progress-meter.objective: Create progress and meter elements with numeric values, ranges, and fallback text.
html-progress-meter.hint: Both elements should include fallback text between their tags.
checks: Progress has numeric value and max
Meter has numeric range and value

html-template.title: Prepare inert reusable markup
html-template.summary: template stores markup that is not rendered immediately. Scripts can clone it later.
html-template.objective: Create a template with a non-empty id containing an article with an h2.
html-template.hint: Nest article and h2 inside template.
checks: Named template contains article card markup

html-dialog.title: Create a native dialog
html-dialog.summary: dialog represents modal or non-modal dialog content and provides native semantics.
html-dialog.objective: Create an open dialog containing an h2 and a close button with type="button".
html-dialog.hint: Add open for preview and nest the heading and button.
checks: Open dialog contains its title and close button

html-code-pre.title: Show code as code
html-code-pre.summary: code marks computer code. pre preserves whitespace and line breaks for preformatted text.
html-code-pre.objective: Create a pre element containing a code element with any short code sample.
html-code-pre.hint: Nest code inside pre, not the other way around.

html-description-meta.title: Summarize the page for search
html-description-meta.summary: A meta description summarizes page content for search engines and link previews.
html-description-meta.objective: Add a meta description in head with non-empty content that summarizes the page.
html-description-meta.hint: Put the meta tag inside head.
checks: Meta description has content in head

html-canonical.title: Declare the canonical URL
html-canonical.summary: A canonical URL tells search engines which URL is the preferred version of a page.
html-canonical.objective: Add a canonical link in head that points to an absolute http or https URL.

html-safe-scripts.title: Load scripts without blocking
html-safe-scripts.summary: defer avoids blocking HTML parsing for classic scripts. Module scripts defer automatically. noscript explains what happens without scripting.
html-safe-scripts.objective: In head, load one deferred classic script and one module script. In body, add noscript fallback text.
html-safe-scripts.hint: Put both script tags in head and noscript in body.
checks: Deferred classic script exists in head

html-full-page.title: Assemble an accessible page
html-full-page.summary: A production page combines semantic structure, accessible navigation, meaningful content, metadata, and usable forms.
html-full-page.objective: Build a complete page body with a skip link, header/nav, main article, labelled signup form, and footer.
html-full-page.hint: Choose an id for main, point the skip link to that id, and nest the article and form inside main.
checks: Header contains labelled navigation with a link
Main target contains article and signup form
